summary:
[  edit  ]
The Spring  SOP  deforms and moves the input geometry using spring "forces" on the edges of polygons and on masses attached to each point.
Geometry is deformed using forces that simulate simple physics on the points and edges. A simulated "mass" is assigned to each point. Its primitive edges act as "springs" which oppose the forces, and pull the points back toward their original positions. When the springs are stretched by the forces, they try to pull the points back. The points do not stop moving when they return to their original positions, however, but continue to oscillate because of their mass, until the oscillation dies out.
Forces which act upon the points are as follows:
external force (gravity)
wind (similar to external force)
turbulence (chaotic forces)   The greater the drag value, or smaller the mass, the faster the oscillation dies out.

parameters.label: Preroll Time
parameters.name: timepreroll
parameters.description: How many seconds of the simulation to bypass, after the reset time is reached. For example, if you put the number 33 into this field (and reset is at  $TSTART ), frame one will show the simulation that was at a time of 33 seconds. In other words, the first thirty-two seconds have been bypassed, and the time at thirty-three seconds is shifted to frame one. The first thirty-two seconds must still be calculated in order to compute the status of the points, so you will notice some delay upon reset.

parameters.label: Time Inc
parameters.name: timeinc
parameters.description: The  Time Inc  parameter determines how often to cook the  SOP . By default, this parameter is set to  1/$ FPS  . This means that the  SOP  will cook once for every frame. When complex dynamics are involved, the  SOP  may require more frequent cooking for increased mathematical accuracy. To get sub-frame accuracy in the cooking, set the  Time Inc  to something smaller than  1/$ FPS   . For example, setting the  Time Inc  to  0.5/$ FPS   will mean that the  SOP  gets cooked twice for every frame.

parameters.label: Accurate Moves
parameters.name: accurate
parameters.description: This option makes the nodes move more accurately between frames by calculating their trajectories for fractional frame values.

parameters.label: Attractor Use
parameters.name: attractmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Describes how attractor points are assigned to each particle.

parameters.label: All Points
parameters.name: all
parameters.description: All point attractors affect all particles (or points).

parameters.label: Single Point per Particle
parameters.name: single
parameters.description: When enabled, each particle is assigned a single attractor point, and is affected by only that point. Assignment is done by point number modulo the total number of attractor points.

parameters.label: Reset
parameters.name: reset
parameters.description: While On resets the spring effect of the  SOP .

parameters.label: Reset  Pulse
parameters.name: resetpulse
parameters.description: Instantly reset the spring effect.

parameters.label: External Force
parameters.name: external
parameters.description: ⊞  - Forces of gravity acting on the points. When drag is zero, the points can accelerate with no limit on their speed.

parameters.label: Wind
parameters.name: wind
parameters.description: ⊞  - Wind forces acting on the points. Similar to external force. Using wind (and no other forces, such as turbulence), the points will not exceed the wind velocity.

parameters.label: Turbulence
parameters.name: turb
parameters.description: ⊞  - The amplitude of turbulent (chaotic) forces along each axis. Use positive values, if any.

parameters.label: Turb Period
parameters.name: period
parameters.description: A small period means that the turbulence varies quickly over a small area, while a larger value will cause points close to each other to be affected similarly.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Random number seed for the simulation.

parameters.label: Fixed Points
parameters.name: fixed
parameters.description: This is a point group. All points in the point group will remain unaffected by the forces. Also see the  Group SOP  for notes on how to specify point ranges.

parameters.label: Fixed Points go to Source Positions
parameters.name: revertfixed
parameters.description: Determines whether or not points in the  Fixed Points  group should be moved to the positions of the corresponding points in the Source geometry.

parameters.label: Copy Groups from Source
parameters.name: copygroups
parameters.description: Determines if the Spring  SOP  should copy groups from the Source geometry at each frame. This lets you specify the name of an animating group in the  Fixed Points  field, and the contents of this group will be kept up to date.

parameters.label: Add Mass Attribute
parameters.name: domass
parameters.description: When selected, the  Mass  is computed for the deforming geometry.

parameters.label: Mass
parameters.name: mass
parameters.description: Mass  of each point. Heavier points take longer to get into motion, and longer to stop.

parameters.label: Add Drag Attribute
parameters.name: dodrag
parameters.description: When selected, the geometry is deformed by the  Drag  attribute.

parameters.label: Drag
parameters.name: drag
parameters.description: Drag  of each point.

parameters.label: Spring Behavior
parameters.name: springbehavior
parameters.description: ⊞  - How the springs will behave:

parameters.label: Hooke's Law
parameters.name: hooke
parameters.description: Springs will work according to Hooke's Law. This is generally more stable than  Normalized Displacement .

parameters.label: Hooke's Law : Force = Displacement  Spring constant     Normalize Displacement
parameters.name: normalize
parameters.description: Similar to  Hooke's Law  except that the displacement is normalized to the original length of the Spring.

parameters.label: Spring Constant
parameters.name: springk
parameters.description: The spring constant. How tight the springs are. Increase this value to make the springs tighter and thus make the object more rigid. As this number becomes higher, the springs can oscillate out of control. Decrease the  Time Inc  if this happens.

parameters.label: Initial Tension
parameters.name: tension
parameters.description: The Initial k constant of the geometry before being deformed by the spring operation.

parameters.label: + Limit Plane
parameters.name: limitpos
parameters.description: ⊞  - The points will bounce off the limit planes when it reaches them. The six limit plane fields define a bounding cube. The default settings are one thousand units away, which is very large. Reduce the values to about one to see the effect.

parameters.label: - Limit Plane
parameters.name: limitneg
parameters.description: ⊞  - The points will bounce off the limit planes when it reaches them. The six limit plane fields define a bounding cube. The default settings are one thousand units away, which is very large. Reduce the values to about one to see the effect.

parameters.label: Hit Behavior
parameters.name: hit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Control over what happens when the geometry hits either the six collision planes or the collision object. The options are:

parameters.label: Bounce on Contact
parameters.name: bounce
parameters.description: Geometry will bounce upon contact with the Collision input.

parameters.label: Stick on Contact
parameters.name: stick
parameters.description: Geometry will stick to the Collision input upon contact.

parameters.label: Gain Tangent
parameters.name: gaintan
parameters.description: Friction parameters which can be regarded as energy-loss upon collision. The first parameter affects the energy loss (gain) perpendicular to the surface. 0 means all energy (velocity) is lost, 1 means no energy is lost perpendicular to surface. The second parameter is the energy gain tangent to the surface.

parameters.label: Gain Normal
parameters.name: gainnorm
parameters.description: Friction parameters which can be regarded as energy-loss upon collision. The first parameter affects the energy loss (gain) perpendicular to the surface. 0 means all energy (velocity) is lost, 1 means no energy is lost perpendicular to surface. The second parameter is the energy gain tangent to the surface.

parameters.label: num_points
parameters.description: Number of points in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_prims
parameters.description: Number of primitives in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_particles
parameters.description: Number of particles in this  SOP .

parameters.label: last_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating geometry data on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: last_meta_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating meta surface geometry data (such as metaballs or nurbs) on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: The
parameters.name: Frames
parameters.description: per-Second that TouchDesigner's  Timeline  runs at. Set with  project.cookRate .

parameters.description: type parameter, such as Reset parameter in a  Speed CHOP . A pulse from a CHOP is typically a 0 to 1 to 0 signal in an exported channel.
